+ W.P.(C) 6736/2023 & Cm Appl. 26348/2023
 S Daya Singh And Sons Huf ....

Through: Mr. D. Hasija, Adv.
 versus
 Delhi Development Authority .....Respond
 Through: Ms. Manika Tripat
 Counsel with
 Vashist and Mr.
 Advs.
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Tara Vitasta Ganju
 Order
% 18.05.2023 [Physical Hearing/Hybrid Hearing (as per request)]
1. This matter has been listed before Court on urgent mentioning.

CM APPL. 26348/2023 [For Exemption]
2. Allowed, subject to the Petitioner filing legible copies of the annexures, at least three days before the next date of hearing.

W.P.(C) 6736/2023 3. The grievance of the Petitioner as articulated in the prayers of the Writ Petition which reads as follows:
"(i) issue an appropriate writ, order or direction to the respondent not to interfere in the peaceful and settled possession of the petitioner in property con1prised in Khasra Nos.443(4-16), 444( 4-16), 445(3-1 0), 446(3-0), 447 Min.( 1-4 ), 430/2(0-5), 431/1 (0-1 0), total admeasuring 18 Bighas and 8 Bighas, situated in the Revenue Village Shayoorpur, Tehsil Saket, South Delhi - 110074, now properly known as Farm No.2,
Faith Arena, Shayoorpur, Chattarpur Extn., Satbari, New Delhi- 110074.

(ii) issue an appropriate writ, order or direction against the persons/ officials who have been visiting the property or the petitioner being Farm No.2, Faith Arena,
Shayoorpur, Chattarpur Extn., Satbari, New Delhi - 110074, illegally and unauthorizedly, without any permission or order.
This is a digitally signed order.

4.

Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the Petitioner submits that the Petitioner purchased the property, comprising in Khasra Nos.443(4-16), 444(4-16), 445(3-10), 446(3-0), 44 7 Min.(1-4),
430/2(0-5), 431/1 (0-10), total admeasuring 18 Bighas and 8 Bighas, situated in the Revenue Village Shayoorpur, Tehsil Saket, South Delhi-110074 [hereinafter referred to as "the said Land"], from the erstwhile owner Smt. Shanti Devi by four separate sale deeds, all dated 16.06.1992 registered with the Sub Registrar- II, Delhi/ New Delhi.
5. Learned Counsel for the Petitioner submits that he has received the possession of the said Land on 04.08.1989 by a letter of possession executed by the previous owner in favour of the Petitioner.

5.1 It is further submitted that the Petitioner is in undisputed and undisturbed possession of the said Land since 1989 and, in this regard, seeks to rely on the photographs which he has handed over in Court today.

6. Learned Counsel for the Petitioner further submits that since acquisition proceedings had been initiated against the said Land under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 [hereinafter referred to as "the Act"], an Award bearing No. 10/87-88 [hereinafter referred to as "the Land Acquisition Award"] was rendered under the Act with respect to the said Land.

Since despite the Land Acquisition Award, there was no compensation offered to the Petitioner nor was it tendered by the concerned authority, the Petitioner filed a Petition being W.P.(C) 467/2015 before this W.P.(C)
6736/2023 page 2 of 4 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 14:25:13 Court seeking a declaration qua the acquisition proceedings under the Act.

6.1 By a Judgment passed by a Division Bench of this Court on 22.01.2018 in the said Petition i.e., W.P.(C) 467/2015,
the Court held that the Petitioner was entitled to a declaration and that the acquisition proceedings with regard to the said Land are deemed to have lapsed.

6.2 Learned Counsel for the Petitioner submits that this Judgment of a Division Bench of this Court was however stayed by the Supreme Court by an order dated 22.10.2018 in a Special Leave Petition [SLP] filed by the Respondent.
It is submitted that the said SLP is still pending.

7. Learned Counsel for the Petitioner further submits that for the last two months, officials of Respondent have been visiting and entering the said Land illegally, and in an unauthorised manner,
and are threatening to take over possession of the said Land citing the Land Acquisition Award.

sentences.text:
8. Learned Standing Counsel appearing, on advance notice, on behalf of the Respondent submits that so far as concerns the possession of the said Land, the same was always with the Respondent.
She relies on paragraphs 5 and 6 of the Judgment dated 22.01.2018 which sets forth an extract of the Counter-Affidavit filed by the Land Acquisition Collector (LAC) to submit that the DDA is in an undisputed possession.
9. Learned Counsel for the Petitioner once again relies on the photographs filed to show possession of the said Land.
10. The matter requires further examination.
11. Issue Notice.
12. Learned Counsel for the Respondent submits that she shall file a W.P.(C) 6736/2023 page 3 of 4 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 14:25:13 Counter-Affidavit with respect to the prayers made by the Petitioner in the present Petition.

13. Let a Counter-Affidavit be filed within two weeks.
14.
Rejoinder, if any, will be filed before the next date of hearing.
15. Learned Counsel for the parties shall also file documents qua the present position of the proceedings pending before the Supreme Court in SLP No. 24580/2018.

16. List the matter on 14.07.2023.
17.
In the meantime, the parties shall maintain status quo till the next date of hearing qua the said Land.
18. Needless to add, that if any action is taken qua the subject property, it shall be taken in accordance with the due process of law.
19. The Registry is directed to scan and upload the copies of the pictures handed over in Court today [mentioned in para 5.1 hereinabove], so that it remains embedded in the case file.
20. Parties will act based on the digitally signed copy of the order.
